Five Apple Watch models can measure your blood pressure and alert you when you may be developing high blood pressure, but they don't give you actual blood pressure readings.

Some smart rings and other fitness devices can do this too, but they need regular calibration with a traditional cuff blood pressure monitor. The upcoming Signal Ring claims to offer full blood pressure measurement without any calibration, and says clinical trials involving thousands of people support this claim...

"Silent killer"

Both abnormally high blood pressure (hypertension) and abnormally low blood pressure (hypotension) carry serious health risks.

Of the two, high blood pressure is more dangerous, earning it the name "silent killer," because it can cause serious and irreversible damage to your arteries, heart and brain with no obvious symptoms. Often, the condition isn't discovered until it triggers a heart attack or stroke.

Especially for older adults, regular blood pressure monitoring is ideal. Home cuff blood pressure monitors are available for purchase, making self-measurement convenient. However, fully automated monitoring through a fitness device you wear every day would be even better.

Apple Watch blood pressure feature

The launch of watchOS 26 has enabled five Apple Watch models to measure blood pressure:

  • Apple Watch Series 11
  • Apple Watch Series 10
  • Apple Watch Series 9
  • Apple Watch Ultra 3
  • Apple Watch Ultra 2

However, these models won't give you any readings—they'll only alert you when they detect signs that you may be developing high blood pressure. Other devices like the Oura Ring work in a similar way.

Some fitness devices on the market can provide actual blood pressure readings, but they need regular calibration using measurements from a cuff blood pressure monitor.

Signal Ring

Startup Vital Signals says its smart ring, called the Signal Ring, can match the accuracy of a traditional upper-arm cuff blood pressure monitor without any calibration needed.

CEO Tom Moss told Bloomberg that he nearly died from undiagnosed high blood pressure himself, which motivated him to start the company.

Signal Ring opens for pre-order later today, ships in October, and is priced at $399 with no subscription required. The companion app shows real-time blood pressure readings and long-term blood pressure trends (as shown in the image above).

Notably, the Oura Ring hasn't received approval from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA), but clinical trials showed the ring delivered accurate blood pressure readings for thousands of participants.

Interestingly, Moss has no interest in marketing the Signal Ring to all consumers. He says this type of feature is best suited for older adults, and people whose doctors have assessed them as being at risk for high blood pressure—the implication being the Signal Ring may not excel at other things (like sleep tracking).
